theme.title: Stars and Surprises
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How many points did Giannis Antetokounmpo score in the 2021 title clincher?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Giannis Antetokounmpo scored a playoff career-high 50 points and added 14 rebounds and five blocks

funFacts.text: Giannis reached the championship series after hyperextending his left knee against Atlanta in the East finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Antetokounmpo went down in game four with a hyperextension to his left knee

funFacts.text: Milwaukee rallied from losing the first two Finals games in Phoenix to claim its long-awaited title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bucks won the next four games

funFacts.text: Jrue Holiday's arrival from New Orleans had bolstered the Bucks' defense before the championship run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bucks acquired guard Jrue Holiday, a highly respected defensive player

questions.prompt: What was Allen Iverson's scoring average during his 2000–01 MVP season?
questions.note: 31.1 a night, enough to lead the league and win MVP.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: All-Star guard Allen Iverson averaged 31.1 points, 4.6 assists and 2.5 steals per game

funFacts.text: Iverson led the NBA not only in scoring but also in steals that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: leading the league in both scoring and steals

funFacts.text: Iverson also won All-Star Game MVP in Washington, D.C., where the East beat the West by a single point.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Iverson scored 25 points along with 5 assists and 4 steals, and was named the All-Star Game Most Valuable Player

funFacts.text: Philadelphia had an unusual awards sweep: teammate Aaron McKie was Sixth Man of the Year and Mutombo was Defensive Player of the Year.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Aaron McKie provided the team with 11.6 points, 5.0 assists and 1.4 steals per game, and was named the NBA Sixth Man of the Year

questions.prompt: How many assists per game did Jimmy Butler average in his first Heat season?
questions.note: 6.0 assists per night as a creative forward.

funFacts.text: Butler collected 103 steals in just fifty-eight appearances.
He averaged 19.9 points while also organizing Miami's offense.
Butler started all fifty-eight regular-season games he played.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jimmy Butler | SF | 58 | 58

questions.prompt: Draymond Green led all scorers in Game 7 of the 2016 Finals. How many points did he score?
questions.note: 32, more than anyone else that night.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Draymond Green put up his best performance of the Finals, leading all scorers with 32 points,

funFacts.text: Green shot an outstanding six of eight from beyond the arc in the final game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: including 6-of-8 from three-point range

funFacts.text: His stat line also included 15 rebounds and nine assists.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: along with 15 rebounds and nine assists

funFacts.text: Kyrie Irving added 26 points for Cleveland during the decisive game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kyrie Irving added 26 points for Cleveland

questions.prompt: Dallas won Game 2 of the 2011 Finals after trailing by how many points?
questions.note: 15, the biggest Finals comeback since Boston rallied from 24 down in 2008.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Mavs' 15-point comeback was the biggest in an NBA Finals game since the 24-point comeback

funFacts.text: Dirk finished the comeback with a driving layup using his injured left hand.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Nowitzki then made a driving layup with his injured left hand with 3.6 seconds left.

funFacts.text: Mario Chalmers briefly tied the game on a three-pointer before Dallas took the decisive possession.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: However, Mario Chalmers tied it with a 3 of his own with 24.5 seconds left

funFacts.text: The Mavericks' victory ended a nine-game home playoff winning streak for Miami.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Mavs' win broke the Heat's 9-game home winning streak in the playoffs
